sections.h2: Which Bakersville offices run Mitchell County property tax?
sections.html:
The county splits the work between an assessor and a collector, and both sit on Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville. Each opens at 8:00 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays.

  • Assessor: Suite 5 at number 26, phone 828.688.2139 extension 1407. This office lists, values and assesses real and personal property.
  • Collector: number 61, phone 828.537.1627. This office sends bills and accepts payment.

The assessor also takes applications for relief, exemptions, exclusions and Present Use Value. The collector's bill includes fire tax for seven fire districts, so the lines on your statement depend on which district your parcel falls in.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau show for Mitchell County?
sections.html:
Mitchell County is a small place. Census estimates give 15,062 people for July 1, 2025, living across 221.25 square miles of land, or about 67 per square mile in 2020. The population was 15,579 in 2010 and 14,903 in 2020.

Owners live in 76.3 percent of homes, and the middle value of those homes is $220,100 in the 2020 to 2024 survey. The county has 6,587 households, a median rent of $813, and a typical commute of 24.4 minutes. About 27.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. Just 44 building permits were counted in 2025.

That older population makes the state relief programs below worth a close look for many local owners.

sections.h2: What is the Mitchell County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
A bill is due September 1, stays free of interest through January 5, and goes delinquent January 6. Interest runs 2 percent for the first month and three quarters of a percent for each following month. A deadline that lands on a weekend slides to the next business day.

Calendar from the Mitchell County Tax Collector's page
Time of yearStep
January 1Assessment date
JanuaryListing month for changes
JulyCurrent bills processed
AugustBills mailed to January 1 owner of record
September 1Payment due
January 5Last interest-free day
FebruaryDelinquent notices go out
MarchDelinquent list advertised

The state rule behind the interest-free cutoff is G.S. 105-360.

sections.h2: Where and how do Mitchell County taxpayers pay?
sections.html:
Walk-in payments at the Tax Office can be cash, check, debit or credit. Online, the county points taxpayers to mitchell.webtaxpay.com for card or e-check payment, and the outside vendor adds a convenience fee.

Monthly installments are allowed on current taxes. Delinquent balances can also be spread out, but only after a payment agreement is signed. Anyone already late should phone 828.537.1627 before the March newspaper advertisement.

The collector gives sellers a clear instruction: the August bill goes to whoever owned the property on January 1, so read the attorney's closing papers to confirm the year was settled. After a mid-year sale, the bill can still show the prior owner's name.

sections.h2: What must a Mitchell County owner report during January?
sections.html:
Report changes to real or personal property during the listing month. The county commissioners may stretch that window, and the assessor says missing it brings a 10 percent penalty. The authority is G.S. 105-307.

The assessor's page names these taxable items:

  • business assets,
  • untagged vehicles,
  • boats and personal watercraft,
  • untagged campers and trailers,
  • mobile homes,
  • aircraft.

Download the forms, fill them in and mail them to the assessor's Suite 5 address. The latest versions come from the state Department of Revenue. New construction, a removed outbuilding or a newly placed manufactured home are changes worth reporting.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Mitchell County valuation?
sections.html:
The county's Board of Equalization and Review hears value complaints, and unless a special board exists the commissioners fill that role. Under G.S. 105-322 it opens between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May.

  • Ask to be heard, in writing or in person, before the board adjourns.
  • If its notice was mailed fewer than 15 days before adjournment, you get 15 days from mailing.
  • Expect the decision by mail within a month of adjournment.
  • A next step to the state Property Tax Commission has a 30-day clock (G.S. 105-290).

Counties must reappraise real estate at least once every eight years, and in a reappraisal year the board stays in session until December 1. Ask the assessor when your parcel was last reappraised and when the next cycle falls.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs fit Mitchell County owners?
sections.html:
The state has three programs, and an owner is limited to one. Each is requested on Form AV-9 from the county assessor.

  • Age or disability exclusion: $25,000 or half of value, whichever is more, for owners 65 or older or permanently disabled with 2026 income no higher than $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 of value, with no age or income limit. A Veterans Service Officer first completes Form NCDVA-9. The Census Bureau counts 946 veterans in Mitchell County.
  • Circuit breaker: tax held to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent up to $58,200 for 2026, after five years of living in the home. A new application is due every year.

Tax deferred under the circuit breaker comes due on a transfer or when the owner stops living in the house, so a seller should ask the assessor for the deferred total. The details appear in G.S. 105-277.1B.

sections.h2: What happens if Mitchell County taxes go unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
The county has a lien on the parcel from the January 1 listing date, with penalties and costs attached (G.S. 105-355). A foreclosure suit under G.S. 105-374 ends in an auction at the courthouse door.

That sale takes time. A report is due within three days, and bidders have 10 days afterward to raise the price or object. Until the court confirms, a person redeeming pays the taxes, penalties, interest and costs. An owner who closes a sale earlier keeps the choice of buyer and price.

For a Mitchell County seller the order of operations is short: ask the collector for a payoff, ask the assessor about any relief or deferral on the parcel, and pass both numbers to the closing attorney. A written cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as-is can fit this timeline when repairs are not an option.

faqs.q: When does interest begin on a Mitchell County bill?
faqs.a: Interest begins January 6. The last interest-free day is January 5, and the charge is 2 percent for the first month plus three quarters of one percent for each month after.

faqs.q: Where do I pay in person?
faqs.a: Use the Tax Collector at 61 Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville, weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30. Cash, check, debit and credit are accepted at the office.

faqs.q: Whom do I call about my assessment or an exemption form?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor handles both, at 828.688.2139 extension 1407. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 5.

faqs.q: May I pay my bill in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, in monthly installments on current-year tax. Late balances can be paid the same way once a payment agreement is signed.

faqs.q: What happens if I forget to list property in January?
faqs.a: The assessor says a 10 percent penalty applies to property left unlisted during the regular period. That period is January unless the commissioners extend it.
